Batches 011, 020 and 021 said the same thing about their own authors, for the same reason.

THE DECISION THIS BATCH TURNS ON, AND IT IS A REFUSAL. §9.1 classifies the published industry catalog `PUBLIC-0` with "Client projection: allowed". RFC-2026-012 §2 says direct client reads go through named `security_invoker` views and never a base table, and §3 says the read allowlist starts empty and grows only by RFC. The allowlist IS still empty -- `exposed_views` measures []. The two do not contradict, and the RFC's own "crux" section is why: it is about which TIER issues a statement, and its finding is that a policy constrains the row's content and the session's identity while saying nothing about the tier. §9.1 is the same kind of statement one level up: it classifies CONTENT and names no object, no tier and no mechanism. RFC-2026-012 names all three and sits at position 1 of the conflict order where the data package sits at 4. So §9.1 licenses the content, RFC-2026-012 licenses the object, and this batch can satisfy only the first. app.industry_packs and app.industry_pack_versions are created with ENABLE and FORCE row level security, NO policy, and NO grant to `authenticated` or `anon`. The catalog exists, is immutable, and is unreachable from the request path.

WHAT THAT COST, STATED RATHER THAN ABSORBED. The client-facing half of §5's industry.core row is NOT implemented and cannot be by a pull request. An RFC that opens the allowlist is larger than it looks: §8.5 requires an exposed view to be `security_invoker = true`, and such a view is evaluated with the CALLER's privileges on the base table -- so the entry is a view AND a column-scoped SELECT grant to `authenticated` AND a SELECT policy admitting it, three objects in one decision. Leaving all three absent is what keeps it one decision instead of three-quarters of one already made in a migration.

WHY THE PRECEDENT OF 010, 020 AND 021 DOES NOT REACH THE GLOBAL TABLES. Those batches grant `authenticated` SELECT on base tables, which RFC-2026-012 §2 also names; that gap is inherited, is recorded in the manifest's blockers, and is not fixed here because migration invariant 1 forbids rewriting a merged migration and the lint A1's condition 2 attaches to DB-00 has not landed. What makes 030 not a repetition of it is that every one of those grants is bounded by a predicate RLS can express -- `app.is_active_member(workspace_id)` -- so a leak reaches one workspace and the isolation suite proves the boundary. A GLOBAL catalog has no such predicate: the only thing between an authenticated caller and the whole table would be the column grant, which is exactly the failure §2 names. §2's reason is prospective on a tenant table and load-bearing here.

`anon` IS GRANTED NOTHING AND THAT IS A REFUSAL TOO. A published catalog is the one family in this schema an anonymous reader could plausibly be given, and §8.5 says anonymous holds no TENANT policy while saying nothing about a global one. Granting it decides that the product has an unauthenticated surface, which is A1 Security's through an RFC. The refusal is asserted on the SCHEMA, so it fails the day anon is granted USAGE on app.

THE TENANT TABLE IS A DIFFERENT ANSWER TO A DIFFERENT QUESTION, and the inference is stated. §8 has NO row for an industry pack anywhere in its four matrices -- RFC-2026-012's own inventory says as much and labels its own row an inference. app.industry_assignments is nevertheless governed by §8.1's two Business rows, because 020's header named the industry pack assignment as part of a Business's attribute surface while deferring it to this batch. So SELECT is active membership (Y for every role), INSERT/UPDATE is owner-or-admin (Y) plus a scoped editor (P), and the member-scope narrowing is one RESTRICTIVE FOR ALL policy. If A1 Data disagrees with that reading, the six policies are where to disagree.

`covers` FOR THE `P` CELL AND `admits` FOR THE NARROWING, which is 021's distinction consumed rather than re-decided. An editor who has never been scoped gains nothing from this batch, and a member holding no scope row is not narrowed by it. Batch 030 introduces no new reading of §7.

ONE CONSEQUENCE OF 021 IS SURFACED RATHER THAN HIDDEN, and it is the result to look at twice. `app.member_scope_covers_business` counts a `page` scope on the Business its Page hangs from -- 021 says so in terms, so that a page-scoped member can reach the Business at all -- and an industry assignment is a Business-level row. So an editor scoped to ONE PAGE can re-pin the whole Business's industry pack. 021 already grants that identity UPDATE on app.business_profiles by the same predicate, so 030 inherits the semantics rather than widening them; narrowing it would mean a different `covers` function, which is an amendment to a merged batch. `page-editor-a-can-repin-the-industry-assignment-of-business-a1` asserts it positively so a reviewer meets it in a case rather than in a footnote.

PUBLISHED IMMUTABLE IS EXPRESSED THE WAY 020 EXPRESSES IT, THREE TIMES. app.industry_pack_versions has no `updated_at` column and no trigger, no UPDATE or DELETE grant to any role, and no UPDATE or DELETE policy -- and 030's apply-time block walks six roles against the live ACLs and the policy catalog and raises if any cell holds either verb. The lifecycle the industry pack contract defines (draft -> candidate -> approved -> active -> deprecated -> retired) is NOT modelled: a mutable status column beside an immutable row is the contradiction 020 refused one column over, so the table records PUBLISHED versions with a NOT NULL `released_at`, and deprecation is owed to the batch that brings a curation command path. Nothing pinned is harmed: an assignment references the immutable row, so "pinned old content ... old result reproducible" holds by construction.

TWO BASELINE FINDINGS RECORDED RATHER THAN GUESSED AT (§15). §5 assigns this family the retention classes `CATALOG/HISTORY` and §10 DEFINES NO `CATALOG` CLASS -- twenty-six rows and none of them that one -- while `HISTORY` is defined as "อายุ Workspace + lineage", which cannot describe a global row that outlives every workspace. No retention window is encoded. And §8's matrices have no row for an industry pack at all, which is why the global tables have no cell to implement and every operation on them is denied by default.

THE FIXTURE GREW BY FOUR SYMBOLS AND EACH ONE HAS A CASE THAT NEEDS IT. `business_a4_unassigned` is the only live Business with no assignment, which the permitted INSERT needs and which no existing Business could be: §4's ERD makes an assignment zero-or-one per Business, so every other live Business must carry one for the scope and cross-tenant negatives to be about a policy rather than a missing row, and business_a3_archived is reserved for §11.3's refusal. `industry_pack_interior` and its two versions are the first fixture rows that belong to NO TENANT, and they carry no `_a` or `_b` suffix for that reason -- every other symbol names the workspace its row lives in. The two versions exist because a re-pin needs a target that is not the version already pinned. Each version's CHECKSUM is computed in SQL from its own catalog symbol rather than pasted, so it is recomputable like every uuid5 here.
